mana.headline: Front Attack Damage Boost first, then Weapon Damage Boost, Critical Damage Boost and Damage Boost.

lines.note: A multiplier of its own. About 58% of your boss damage lands from the front with no Templar in the party, and about 40% beside one. Only Superior and Superior Abyssal Manastones roll it.
Second choice, about equal to the next two.

mana.fill: Fill the other slots with Attack first, then Critical Hit, then Accuracy if you are missing bosses. Each of those is a 10% roll on a stone, so they are what most slots will become.
mana.pvp: Abyssal Manastones swap about a third of every roll for PvP lines such as PvP Attack. Use them only on a PvP set. Builds split on which PvP line to take first, so check what your Abyss gear already has.
extra: Double Chance cannot be rolled by any stone. It comes from the pet, Soul Binding lines on the helmet, shoulders and cape, Impact Hit and Lunge Stance.
If you off-tank a hard fight, one source suggests Block first, then Defense and HP, because Block raises parry and shield block chance. That is role advice, not Gladiator-specific data.
mana.fillShort: Attack, then Critical Hit, then Accuracy

pve.why: Area stones pay out once for every enemy hit, and every damage stone of one grade averages the same damage against a single target. So an area stone is never worse and gets better with each extra enemy. Against one enemy it is worth half as much. A Gladiator fights packs, so this fits. Take the Unique version if you have it.

pvp.why: A 3% chance to stun, up to 3 s at Unique, once every 5 s at most. Meslamtaeda's Greed shuts a player down for a moment.

alt.why: When you off-tank, the only proc that slows how fast the target attacks.

theo.note: Seal and Paralyze lead among top players because their rankings include PvP. Zikel's Vestige and Traufnir's Courage together make fire the most common damage choice.
